title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars
text: A neutron star is the collapsed core of a massive star that has undergone a supernova explosion. They are extraordinarily dense objects, with a mass 1.4 to 3 times that of the Sun compressed into a sphere only about 20 kilometers in diameter. A cubic centimeter of neutron star material would weigh about 400 million tons. Neutron stars rotate rapidly and can emit beams of electromagnetic radiation, in which case they are observed as pulsars. The first pulsar was discovered in 1967 by Jocelyn Bell Burnell. Some neutron stars in binary systems can accrete matter from a companion star, leading to X-ray emission and, in some cases, gamma-ray bursts.
